items.label: Make your AI check its own work
items.text:
The agent doing the work is the worst one to check it. By the end its context is foggy.

So add a reviewer with fresh context. It gets the plan, the contract and your interview answers, then checks every output at every checkpoint. Off brief? Back to the drawing board, rerun, then pass.

Full video on YouTube (link in bio).

#aiagents #claudecode #aiautomation #qualitycontrol #marketingagency

items.label: 6 files that save your AI from a crash
items.text:
A harness is only good while it's running. And crashes happen.

Keep these six files on disk: interview.md, contract.md, plan.md, progress.md, constraints and features.json. After a restart it rereads the contract, loads the skills and carries on from the last checkpoint.

Nothing lost. Full video on YouTube (link in bio).

items.label: Draft 1 · Problem
items.text:
Your Meta ads are getting spend. They're still reaching the wrong people.

Put 6–8 ads in an ad set and only a couple end up getting spend. Even those winners can miss your ideal customer.

Meta's Andromeda engine now pulls buyers in from every stage of the funnel, so who you speak to decides everything.

So before we write a single ad, we research the buyer:
→ the top 3 ideal customer profiles, each with a fit score
→ their fears, desires and the questions they ask before booking
→ real quotes, each with an impact score

For a med spa client, the top profile scored an 88% fit. One fear stood out: someone googles a med spa, calls, gets no answer and books at the place next door instead.

That fear became the hook.

Diagnose before you write. Every creative decision should trace back to a real buyer quote.

The full walkthrough is in the video. Want this built for your business? Book a call: [BOOKING LINK]

#MetaAds #FacebookAds #ICPResearch #AdCopywriting

items.label: Draft 2 · I-Built
items.text:
I built an AI agent that finds your buyers' exact words before we write a single ad.

It's called ICP Research Radar. It researches a business's top 3 ideal customer profiles and scores each one.

For a med spa client, the #1 profile came back at 88% fit, with fears, desires, buyer questions and real-life quotes, each with an impact score.

The part most people miss: one audience isn't one message. In the live report, the audience splits by objection (40%, 25% and 15%), and each slice needs its own angle.

We use that one report for everything downstream: ads, landing pages, emails and video scripts.

Research first. Then write in their words, not yours.

Full walkthrough, including the live report: [YOUTUBE LINK]

#MetaAds #ICPResearch #ClaudeAI #AdCopywriting

AI gets you to 90%. Your buyer's words and your own voice do the rest.

So I recorded myself starting from nothing, and let AI do the thinking with me:

→ I told it I didn't know what to ask, and asked it how to ask better questions
→ I asked one hard question: "How can I get you to 100% confidence that the 10 app ideas are groundbreaking?" Nobody can reach 100%, and that's the point
→ I used reverse prompting: ask AI to ask itself a question, and let it write the prompt
→ I made it score its own work, from 8.5 and 7 towards 9.5, never 10 out of 10

The tools will keep changing. Knowing how to think with AI is the skill that lasts, and it's what makes you valuable to any business.

What does an AI bot actually run in a real business, day to day?

I counted. 28 jobs across two businesses I own, and 10 are worth copying.

Seven in the morning, it test-calls our AI sales reps and scores every answer out of 100 against the wording I approved. At nine, it emails 150 businesses. In the afternoon it ships fixes and new pages to the website. At four, it follows up the people who showed interest.

A few that matter most:

→ Two AI sales reps that make real calls, say they're AI and look up approved answers mid-call
→ A full-time rep for about £752 a month, about £377 realistically
→ 150 emails every weekday, which found 5 warm leads on 22 October
→ 14 new industry pages in one go, built and put live on its own

And the part that makes it safe: anything public waits for my yes. Emails, guides and fixes run on their own. Posts, outreach changes and new wording for the reps do not.

Most AI builds go wrong the same way: you pay for the code first, and find out everyone hates it second.

Prompt. The AI writes code. You pay for the tokens. Then you, your team and your client look at it and hate it.

Then you do it again.

The worst version is when it's already live, writing to your database and sitting in front of your client.

So we flipped the order. Before a single line of production code, I put every screen and every bit of motion on one board in Claude:

→ The brand pack sits at the top, so the AI follows the typography and colours every time.

→ The client sees every click and screen transition, and picks the winners.

→ Every choice goes into a decision register: checked, signed, frozen. Nothing changes without a new decision, and the AI reads what's been signed off.

In this week's Whiteboard Wednesdays I build two boards live for made-up clients: a luxury shoe brand's hero section, where we picked A1 and B1 from three styles and three motion options, and a TRT clinic's landing page with its problem cards, emails and video scripts.

Managing the narrative is 50% of the job. The board is how you do it before the money is spent.
